External view inputs are validated with `isUsageStatus()` before the standalone host renders them. ## Supported local sources | Provider | Source and operation | Multi-account boundary | | --- | --- | --- | | Codex / ChatGPT | Live read through documented local Codex app-server methods | One authenticated `CODEX_HOME` per account; browser connection is implemented | | Claude Code | Last-collected Pro/Max quota from documented status-line JSON | Separate snapshot slot and explicit collector binding per authenticated CLI account environment | | Antigravity CLI | Last-collected per-bucket quota from documented status-line JSON | Separate snapshot slot and explicit collector binding per authenticated CLI account environment | | Cursor team | Reported current-cycle per-user spending through the official team Admin API | Exact team member ID plus an environment credential reference; multiple members and separate team keys supported | Claude and Antigravity collectors do not log in, extract tokens, read credential stores, or query undocumented endpoints. Independent snapshot files prevent one slot from overwriting another; labels alone do not establish distinct upstream identity. Authenticate each CLI environment with the intended account and bind the correct collector to it. Switching an upstream login requires reviewing that binding. Live multi-account authentication for these providers has not been verified. **Personal Cursor subscription quota is not supported.** The team API does not authorize reading unrelated personal subscriptions. Anthropic API billing, Claude Enterprise analytics, Gemini API billing, context-window percentages, and local session token counts are not implemented as subscription quota sources. ## Codex account boundary The first source is Codex usage for ChatGPT-signed-in accounts. The adapter starts one `codex app-server` process per explicitly configured `CODEX_HOME` and calls the documented `account/read` and `account/rateLimits/read` methods. Codex owns login, token refresh, and credential storage. Subset never reads `auth.json`, copies tokens, calls unofficial `wham` endpoints, or accepts API-key billing as ChatGPT subscription usage. Each profile has a local ID and display label; an account signed in with an API key is reported as unsupported. Individual profile failures do not hide successful profiles. The view shows provider-reported used percentage and reset time per returned limit window. Remaining percentage is labeled as a calculation from reported usage. Codex's response-level `ordinaryUsageAllowed` is preserved separately: explicit `false` means `blocked`, even when quota percentages are positive or reset times have elapsed. Missing permission remains unavailable, never inferred from quota. Per-bucket `rateLimitReachedType` and `spendControlReached` are retained even when a bucket has no windows; the five known reached-limit reasons are allowlisted, and unknown or malformed access fields produce partial data. Aggregate permission and per-bucket restrictions remain distinct. These fields were verified against the generated non-experimental protocol of installed Codex CLI 0.159.3 without reading credentials or account state. Banked reset count and earliest known expiry appear only when supplied. Missing observations and partial responses remain visible. Account email and opaque credit IDs are discarded at the adapter boundary. Observation time is captured when app-server returns. The view treats an observation older than five minutes as stale and updates freshness every 30 seconds independently of successful refreshes; source refresh is manual. The text-only fallback likewise includes source, observation time, freshness, calculation qualifiers, access denials, and sanitized failure details. The read request is local and read-only. `agentUsageResult(status)` yields structured data, a text fallback, and a trusted view ID. The isolated Outright SET-1 integration registers a read-only Codex MCP tool with McpFn and an inspector for this view. Its tool and browser behavior require separate host checks before claiming availability. Account connection is an explicit operation in the standalone local host; the capability package does not handle credentials or expose reset redemption, purchases, or other mutations. ## Standalone local preview In the local dashboard, choose **Use current Codex account** to add the existing ChatGPT sign-in, then enter a label and choose **Connect another ChatGPT account**. The host starts the [documented Codex app-server browser login](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) in a new, isolated Codex home. Follow **Continue with ChatGPT** and choose the intended account in the browser. The dashboard polls the login result and adds the account after Codex confirms a ChatGPT sign-in. A browser reload recovers the active sign-in ID, validated link, and state from the same local server, restoring progress and cancellation controls without persisting credentials or login state in browser storage. This recovery does not survive a server restart. Subset never sees or stores OAuth tokens; Codex manages them in its own home. **Remove** unlinks an existing Codex home from the dashboard; for a Subset-managed home it also deletes that local sign-in after explicit confirmation. Cancelling an unfinished login deletes only its newly created home. The host stores profile labels and Codex home paths in `~/.config/subset/codex-profiles.json` with owner-only file permissions. Managed Codex homes live under `~/.local/share/subset/codex-accounts/`, each with owner-only directory permissions. An owner-controlled profile file may also be supplied directly, for example: ```json [ { "id": "personal", "label": "Personal", "codexHome": "/absolute/path/to/personal-codex-home" }, { "id": "work", "label": "Work", "codexHome": "/absolute/path/to/work-codex-home" } ] ``` Each manually added home must already be signed in with its intended ChatGPT account using Codex. `CODEX_HOME=/absolute/path/to/personal-codex-home codex login` is the Codex-managed login path. `--profile` selects a config overlay within one home and is not account isolation. Do not copy auth files between homes. Account email is not stored in profile metadata or sent to the dashboard status view, so labels should distinguish accounts. A second real ChatGPT sign-in has not yet been available for live two-account verification. After `npm run build`, use `npm run status --workspace=@subset/usage-web` for structured JSON or `npm run serve --workspace=@subset/usage-web` for the local view at `http://127.0.0.1:4174`. `SUBSET_USAGE_PROFILES_FILE` selects a different JSON file; the existing `SUBSET_CODEX_PROFILES_FILE` remains a fallback for persisted Codex setups. The default stays `~/.config/subset/codex-profiles.json` and accepts all provider types. `SUBSET_USAGE_DATA_DIR` optionally selects a managed data directory; `SUBSET_USAGE_PORT` changes the loopback port. Stop the server with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. The server binds only to `127.0.0.1`, checks Host and Origin headers, and requires a matching browser Origin for account mutations. This is a local preview, not a published CLI/skill, hosted agent view, or public web app. OpenAI documents Codex app-server authentication for local or open-source applications, with a different authorization path required for commercial or hosted services. ## Claude and Antigravity collectors In **Manage accounts**, choose **Claude Code quota snapshot** or **Antigravity CLI quota snapshot**, give the account a distinct label, and choose **Add snapshot account**. Expand that account's collector setup and use its generated command, which includes its unique local ID and any custom profile file selection. The command reads JSON on stdin, writes an owner-only quota snapshot, and deliberately produces no stdout. Configure that command as `statusLine.command` in the intended Claude Code account environment or Antigravity CLI's `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`. For example, using the absolute host path and generated account ID: ```json { "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "node /absolute/path/to/subset/apps/usage/server.mjs collect --account claude_example" } } ``` Use the generated command verbatim when paths contain spaces. This collector alone renders no status-line text. To retain an existing status line, use a wrapper that passes the same stdin JSON to the collector and existing renderer, without logging or persisting the raw payload. Subset does not edit provider settings automatically. The [Claude Code status-line contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#rate-limit-usage) supplies `rate_limits.five_hour` and `rate_limits.seven_day`, with `used_percentage` and epoch-second `resets_at`. These subscription fields are documented for Pro/Max after the first API response; missing fields remain unavailable. Remaining quota is calculated from reported usage, not inferred from tokens or context size. The [Antigravity CLI status-line contract](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/statusline/) supplies `quota..remaining_fraction`, `reset_time`, optional `reset_in_seconds`, and optional `plan_tier`. Remaining quota is reported, while used percentage is calculated. A countdown reset is anchored to the capture time, not the dashboard refresh time. Snapshots store only allowlisted quota fields and optional plan tier. Emails, transcripts, credentials, workspace paths, and other CLI metadata are discarded. Stored envelopes bind provider and account ID; malformed, cross-account, oversized, or future-dated snapshots are rejected. A startup payload with no usable quota does not overwrite a prior observation. Refresh reloads the last snapshot without changing its capture time; snapshots become stale after five minutes. While a CLI is inactive, the dashboard cannot fetch a new observation. Removing a managed snapshot account deletes its snapshot, not the upstream sign-in; remove the old collector from CLI settings separately. Use one account-bound collector stream per snapshot slot. Snapshot replacement is atomic, but concurrent collectors for the same slot are last-completion-wins rather than capture-time ordered. Their retained observation timestamp is still shown without modification. Collection rechecks the profile after writing so an overlapping account removal does not leave a recreated managed snapshot. ## Cursor team accounts Set a team API key in the environment used to launch the local host, for example under `CURSOR_WORK_TEAM_KEY`, then choose **Cursor team spending**. Enter the environment variable name, not the secret, and the exact encoded member ID (`user_...`) from the team's documented `/teams/members` operation. A second member can reference the same team credential variable; another team uses its own variable. Subset stores only references and IDs in owner-only configuration and omits both from dashboard props and profile-list responses. The source is the [official team Admin API](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api). The adapter calls only the fixed `https://api.cursor.com/teams/spend` endpoint with Basic authentication and bounded pagination/response size/timeouts. It reports on-demand `spendCents`, the included usage value derived from `overallSpendCents - spendCents`, the reported enforced `effectivePerUserLimitDollars` cap, and `subscriptionCycleStart`. An absent cap or cycle end remains unknown; a spending cap is not a personal subscription quota. Authorization failures, missing members, rate limiting, and malformed responses are isolated per account, without exposing credentials or upstream response text. ## Validation and release gaps Run `npm run test --workspace=@subset/usage` and `npm run test --workspace=@subset/usage-web` after the package build, alongside root `npm run check` and `npm run build`. Root checks build the catalog and usage declarations before checking consuming apps, so they do not require pre-existing ignored `dist` exports. Tests exercise synthetic multi-account provider reads, explicit access denials, safe transport failures, separate snapshot collection, normalization, redaction, profile persistence/removal, pending-login recovery, the local CLI, and host Origin checks. These are not proof of real upstream multi-account login, installed CLI compatibility, or live Cursor API authorization. No public or external-agent availability is claimed by these additions. ## Superfunctions reuse review Reviewed current `superfunctions-dev` source, public manifests, and README contracts on 2026-09-29, plus npm package versions. `authfn@0.3.0` is for owned session/auth flows; Codex app-server already owns this local account login. `@datafn/client@0.1.1` adds synced persistence that this slice does not need. `plugfn@0.1.0` targets third-party service connections, while this source is a local documented Codex process. `@mcpfn/core@0.0.5` is used by the isolated Outright MCP adapter; the capability itself remains host independent. `@uifn/components-svelte@0.0.1` and React equivalent were evaluated; this view currently needs only semantic HTML and a progress element, so no generic primitive dependency was added. `@superfunctions/observability@0.0.1` was evaluated; the connector avoids logging account data and has no telemetry runtime. **Package/version used in this package: none.** Gaps: hosted agent rendering, live two-account verification, and a release-ready hosted account authorization path remain. The multi-provider extension additionally reviewed `plugfn/core` implementation, manifest and README, the provider manifest and readiness matrix, and `authfn/core` implementation, manifest and README on 2026-10-01. Published `plugfn@0.1.0` has no supported Cursor provider and requires an auth/database/encrypted persistent connection runtime; `authfn@0.3.0` owns application sessions, not externally issued team API keys or CLI snapshots. Neither is used. The local alternative remains fixed-endpoint read-only collection with environment credential references, not a competing OAuth or connection framework. The package is private. A future npm release requires the `@sub-set/` scope, versioned exports, a release process, and separate verification.

Standard OpenTelemetry exporter variables (`OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL`, `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS`, `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`, `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, and signal-specific variants) are also supported. See [Monitoring](/docs/en/monitoring-usage) for configuration details.

Set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY` and the OpenTelemetry variables that turn on export, choose its destination, or capture content in your shell, user settings, or managed settings. Claude Code [ignores them in project and local settings](/docs/en/settings-reference#variables-claude-code-ignores-in-env), apart from the off values that section describes. `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` and the export interval, timeout, and compression variables, such as `OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL`, still apply from project and local settings.

## What the subprocess environment scrub removes

When you set [`CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB`](#variables) to `1`, Claude Code removes credentials from the environments of the subprocesses it starts, such as Bash commands, hooks, and stdio MCP servers. This reduces what a prompt injection attack can read. The Claude Code process keeps the credentials for its own API calls.

The scrub recognizes a credential by its variable name or by the shape of its value, so use it as one layer alongside narrow [permission rules](/docs/en/permissions) rather than as the only control.

The table shows what the scrub does to example variables:

| Example variable | What the scrub does |
| :- | :- |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Removes it |
| `NPM_TOKEN`, `DB_PASSWORD` | Removes it, because the name looks like a credential |
| `DATABASE_URL` that contains a password | Removes it, because the value looks like a credential |
| `PIP_INDEX_URL` or `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY` that contains a password | Keeps the URL and cuts the username and password from it |
| `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` | Removes it |
| `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `GH_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_TOKEN` | Leaves it in place, so that `gh` and scripts that call the GitHub API keep working |

Aside CLI 1.26.916.1741 · Skill version 3

# Aside

Aside is an AI browser. Inside Aside, there is an intelligent agent designed to handle complex tasks across user's credentials, cookies, browsing history, and various websites the user uses.

There are two ways of controlling Aside browser:
- `aside exec` delegates the task to Aside agent. Recommended for most tasks- think of it like spawning subagent.
- `aside repl` starts JS REPL session that provides Playwright-compatible. ONLY USE IT when you need to inspect screenshot and DOM directly.

`aside --help` and `aside <command> --help` print current flags and examples.

## Browser usage

### A. Using `aside exec` (Recommended)

It starts a task in a separate session by Aside agent. Use this for most tasks- it's more context efficient and has a lot of skills and memories about user's context.
After spawning the task, watch the run and give the user a status update around every 60 seconds.

```bash
aside "Send reply to Jack in Slack #develop channel: <text>"
aside -m openai/gpt-5.6-sol -s fast --effort high "Create a project in Vercel and return the project URL"
aside --account u1 "Check unread Slack notifications"
aside --permission full-access "Install the CLI from the project README"
aside "https://example.com" # a link starts with http(s) opens website in user's browser screen
```

#### Resuming the task

When you ask follow-up requests or steer / stop the task during the run, use the following commands:

```bash
aside session resume <id>
aside session resume <id> "Continue the search"
aside session steer <id> "Switch to Google Flights"
aside session queue <id> "Export the final list to CSV"
aside session stop <id>
aside session archive <id>
aside session delete <id>
```

`steer` redirects a running turn. `queue` schedules instructions after the current step. Both commands print `ok` and exit.
`aside session list` includes sessions that were not saved to the chat list.

#### Persistence

Sessions stay off the chat list by default. `aside settings save-sessions true` keeps them there.
`aside settings set-default-profile u1` makes later CLI commands use that profile. One-shot override: `--account u1`.

### B. Use `aside repl`

Use this when you need to directly control tabs, inspect screenshot and DOM, and run JavaScript code on the browser.

**Before using `aside repl`, run `aside guide repl` and read its output.**

## Memory

Aside has an accurate memory system for user, which distills user's context into plain-Markdown files who they are, people, projects, sites, preferences).
When you need a user's personal context, always query it before asking the user about prior context, with `aside memory` command:

```bash
aside memory search "<query>" --json
aside memory list --json
aside memory show MEMORY.md
aside memory path
```

Never edit memory files yourself. If the user wants Aside to remember something, run it through `aside exec`.
On `aside mcp`, prefer the `memory_search` tool instead of CLI command.

## Remote control

If user's Aside runs on a remote machine (e.g., this host is Linux but user runs Aside on their macOS laptop), you can control it with following commands:

```bash
aside host list
aside exec --host <id-or-name> "..."
aside repl --host <id-or-name>
aside host use <host>
```

Aside CLI 1.26.916.1741 · Skill version 3

# Before using REPL, read Aside built-in skills first

Aside ships skills for services it already knows how to drive — Slack, Gmail, Notion, Google Docs/Sheets/Search, YouTube, LinkedIn, iMessage, and Aside itself. Each one documents a ready-made REPL global (`slack`, `gmail`, `notion`, ...) that works inside `aside repl`, so check for one before driving a site through `snapshot()` by hand:

```bash
aside skills list
aside skills show <name>
```

Read the matching skill first, then follow it. Tell the user which Aside skill you are using and for what.

# `aside repl` command usage

Run Playwright-style JavaScript in a persistent sandboxed REPL context to interact with Aside Browser.

## Environment

- ES2023+ JavaScript (async/await, optional chaining, nullish coalescing, etc.)
- Playwright API available
- 120 second timeout
- No default modules. No external modules are allowed: no `import` and `require`

**`const`/`let` bindings persist across calls, so always use fresh variable names.**

Available globals:

- `page`: current Playwright-like `Page`.
- `tabs`: open pages in this REPL session.
- `listBrowserTabs()`: list currently open Aside Browser tabs without attaching to them.
- `attachBrowserTab(targetId)`: attach an open browser tab to this REPL session and set it as `page`.
- `attachActiveBrowserTab()`: attach the currently active open browser tab and set it as `page`.
- `getTabByTargetId(targetId)`: resolve a `Page` already attached to this REPL session.
- `openTab(url)`: open a tab, wait until interactive, and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `closeTab(tab)`: close a tab and update `page` and `tabs`.
- `snapshot(page, options?)`: primary page-reading API; returns `{ tree, diff }`.
- `annotatedScreenshot(page)`, `page.screenshot()`: visual verification.
- `page.pdf(options?)`: print the current page to PDF; save user-visible PDFs under `./artifacts/`, e.g. `await page.pdf({ path: './artifacts/page.pdf', format: 'A4' })`.
- `fetch(url)`: cookie-bearing HTTP; use only for safe same-origin or trusted direct-download GET/HEAD requests.
- `fs`, `path`, `Buffer`, `sleep`, `display`, `pwd`.

Always use `console.log()` to return values to yourself.

## Browser interaction with REPL

### Open browser tabs

`aside repl` starts as a neutral session. Do not assume `page` is the user's current tab.

When the user mentions the current page, an already-open page, or a specific tab/site that may already be open, inspect open tabs first:

```js
const openTabs = await listBrowserTabs();
console.log(openTabs.map((tab) => ({ targetId: tab.targetId, active: tab.active, title: tab.title, url: tab.url })));
```

- Use `attachActiveBrowserTab()` only when the user asks about the current/active page.
- Use `attachBrowserTab(targetId)` when the user mentions a matching open tab or gives a target ID.
- After attaching, read with `snapshot(page, { interactive: true })`.

content.text:
I fixed the issues the review turned up, and multi-account Claude Code is now tied to separate Claude config directories. Claude Code support already existed, but nothing linked a Claude slot to a particular sign-in. The checks, both builds and all 79 tests pass (57 in `@subset/usage`, 22 in `@subset/usage-web`). The preview at http://127.0.0.1:4174/ has been restarted on the new code. Nothing is committed.

**Claude Code with multiple accounts**
- Claude Code's documented way to run accounts side by side is one `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` per account. For example, `~/.claude` for your default account, and `~/.claude-work` started with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude`.
- When you add a Claude account you can now enter its config directory. Two accounts can't share one.
- Each account's setup section shows the command to start Claude Code for that account, the path of its `settings.json`, and the `statusLine` JSON to paste into it.
- The collector rejects a snapshot that comes from a different config directory. It identifies the directory from the session transcript path, falling back to the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` variable. Claude Code can strip that variable from child processes, which is why the transcript path is checked first.
- If neither signal is present, the snapshot is accepted. Accounts added without a directory work as before, with no check. The transcript path is used only for the check and is never stored.

**Fixes from the review**
1. **Sign-in race:** cancelling a ChatGPT sign-in while it was still starting could bring it back as active. Finished sign-ins also stayed in memory forever; they're now cleared when a new one starts.
2. **Codex messages:** if Codex sent its own request with the same ID as one of ours, both Codex clients took it as the answer to our request. They now ignore those messages.
3. **Error messages:** a blocked or empty response showed "Unexpected end of JSON input". The UI now shows a readable message instead.
4. **Server restart:** a sign-in left pending across a restart kept the form disabled and showed an error every 2 seconds. It now clears with a clear message.
5. **Shutdown:** Ctrl-C could hang while the browser held connections open. It now closes them and exits within 5 seconds; the restart just now took about 200ms.
6. **Display:** windows read "10080 minute window" and now say "7-day window". The page title was "Codex usage" and is now "Usage · Subset".

New tests cover the Claude directory rule, cancelling during startup, the Codex message guard, and the server and collector command paths. `packages/usage/README.md` and `docs/architecture.md` are updated. In the browser I checked the new Claude field without saving anything, so your accounts are unchanged.

**Not verified or not done:**
- **Real second account:** no second real Claude or ChatGPT account has been signed in end to end.
- **Transcript location:** that transcripts live under `<config dir>/projects/` is what I see on this machine, not something the docs state.
- **Claude spend limit:** Claude Code also reports a spend-limit value when it runs behind a company gateway, and that value can go above 100%. I left it out.
- **Antigravity limit:** an Antigravity account reporting exactly 32 quota buckets is marked "partial", because the code can't tell 32 from more than 32 that got cut off.

content.text:
The dashboard now shows your default Claude Code account automatically. It's live at http://127.0.0.1:4174/ as **Claude Code (default)**, showing your `team` plan and "Signed in to Claude Code". It has no quota numbers yet. All tests, `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass, and I checked the page in the browser.

**How it works**
- On each refresh the server runs `claude auth status --json`, Claude Code's own command. If your default config directory (`~/.claude`, or `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` if set) is signed in, the account is added automatically.
- Subset keeps only the sign-in state, the sign-in method, the plan and the directory. Your email and organization ID are thrown away, and Subset never reads Claude credentials.
- Every Claude account tied to a config directory now shows its plan and sign-in state on each refresh. A signed-out directory shows as unauthorized, and an API-key sign-in shows that subscription quota isn't available.
- If you remove the default account, it stays removed. A new **Use default Claude Code account** button adds it back.
- The new Claude CLI reader lives in `packages/usage/src/claude.ts`, with new tests in `packages/usage/test/claude.test.mjs`. The server test uses a fake `claude`, so it can never pick up your real account.

**Why there are no quota numbers yet**
1. **Collector not set up:** quota still comes only from the status-line collector. Your `~/.claude/settings.json` already has a status line installed by Orca. I haven't changed that file, because Subset's rule is not to edit provider settings automatically. The fix is a small wrapper that sends the same input to both Orca's script and Subset's collector. I can add that if you want, though Orca may rewrite its own entry later.
2. **Team plan:** Claude Code's docs say quota fields are sent only to Pro and Max subscribers, and to accounts behind a company gateway with a spend limit. Your account is on a Team plan, so the quota may never arrive. The card would then say quota is unavailable for this plan. We'd only know for sure after wiring the collector and running a session.

Nothing is committed.

content.text:
I've redesigned the usage dashboard in the style of Usage Buddy and added a few things it lacks. The whole page now uses Twenty One Native from `@21n/fonts@1.0.1`. The new version is live at http://127.0.0.1:4174/; reload the page to see it. Checks, both builds and all 87 tests pass. Nothing is committed.

**Why the Claude card looked like that:** your Claude account is signed in, but no quota snapshot has reached Subset yet. Claude Code only sends quota numbers to a status-line command, and `~/.claude/settings.json` still runs only Orca's status line. The old screen treated "waiting for the first snapshot" as an error, so it showed a red message, an "Unavailable" badge and "Observed Unavailable". The card now shows an amber **Waiting for data** pill with a **Set up collector** link.

**What changed:**
- **Top bar:** Usage logo with an account count, a "Checked just now" time, Refresh (or press `r`), an auto-refresh menu (off, 5, 15 or 30 min; default 5, paused while the tab is hidden), and **Add account**.
- **Summary strip:** how many accounts need attention, the next reset across all accounts, and the highest usage.
- **Account cards:** a provider tile, a plain-language status pill (Up to date, Waiting for data, Partial data, Signed out, Limited), and the plan ("Codex · Pro", "Claude Code · Team").
- **Usage rows:** readable names like "Weekly usage" instead of "codex · primary", 20-segment meters coloured green, amber or red, and countdowns like "Resets in 5d 17h" with the exact time on hover.
- **Pace estimate (Usage Buddy doesn't have this):** your Codex card currently says "≈ runs out in 1d 3h at this pace". You've used 52% of the week in about 1.3 days, so the estimate is genuinely that you'll run out early. It's always marked as an estimate.
- **Dialogs instead of the long form:**
  - **Add account:** a provider picker, plus one-click buttons to use the Codex and Claude sign-ins already on this computer.
  - **Account settings (the ⋯ button):** the account's details, numbered collector setup steps with Copy buttons, a ready-made wrapper script for people who already have a status line, and Remove with an in-dialog confirmation.
- **Also:** light and dark themes that follow your system setting, toast messages, keyboard and screen-reader labels, a single-column phone layout, and a proper empty state. The labels for source, observation time and calculated "≈" values are all still there.

The display logic moved into a new tested module, `packages/usage/src/present.ts`, and the README describes the new view.

**Not checked yet:**
- **Dark mode:** I couldn't switch the test browser to dark mode, so I've only looked at light mode.
- **Claude quota numbers:** Claude Code's docs say quota is sent only for Pro and Max plans (or behind a company gateway), and yours is Team. Even with the collector set up, the card may stay at "Waiting for data". Getting a Claude Code session to report quota is the only way to know. I can add the wrapper to `~/.claude/settings.json` so it runs next to Orca's status line, but that means editing your settings, so I'll wait for your go-ahead.

content.text:
Collector setup is now automatic: one **Install collector** click replaces the copy-paste steps. The page also uses Phosphor icons and an ECharts trend chart. Checks, both builds and all 91 tests pass. The preview at http://127.0.0.1:4174/ is running the new code; reload to see it. Nothing is committed.

**How the automation works**
- **Install collector** appears on the card, in the account's settings, and as a checkbox when you add an account with a config directory. Clicking it writes the collector into that account's `settings.json`, for example `/Volumes/OS - Data/…/claude-serro/settings.json`.
- **Before writing,** Subset saves a backup as `settings.json.subset-backup` and keeps every other setting. A file that isn't valid JSON is never rewritten.
- **Existing status lines keep working.** If the file already has one (your `~/.claude` has Orca's), Subset saves it and runs it after each capture with the same input, so its display doesn't change. I tested this end to end.
- **Uninstall** puts the previous status line back, and so does removing the account. If another tool later overwrites the entry, the settings dialog shows "Replaced by another tool" with a **Reinstall** button.
- **Still manual:** an account with no config directory can't be installed automatically, because Subset can't tell which settings file belongs to it. The manual steps are under "Set up manually" in its settings.

Both your Claude accounts currently show **Not installed**. I haven't clicked Install, since it edits your real settings files. That's your call; one click per account does it.

**Icons**

Before this change they were hand-drawn SVGs and two-letter tiles like "Cx" and "Cl". They're now Phosphor (`phosphor-svelte@3.1.0`), and the provider tiles use plain Phosphor symbols, not company logos:

| Provider | Phosphor icon |
|---|---|
| Codex | OpenAI logo |
| Claude | asterisk |
| Antigravity | planet |
| Cursor | cursor |

**Charts**

Apache ECharts (`echarts@6.1.0`) draws a usage trend line on each card. A trend needs past data, so the server now keeps a local history in `usage-history.json`: only account IDs, times and percentages, kept for 8 days, readable only by you. A card shows its chart once an account has three readings spanning at least 30 minutes. With auto-refresh on, your real charts will appear after about half an hour. The chart code loads only when needed, so the first page load stayed at 167 KB.

Neither package exists in Superfunctions, which the README now records.

**Still unverified:**
- **Dark mode:** I couldn't switch the test browser to dark mode, so I haven't seen the dark theme.
- **Chart check used sample data:** I checked the chart with sample history on a second, separate server, not with your real readings.
- **Claude quota on your plan:** both Claude accounts are on a Team plan, and Claude Code's docs say quota is only sent for Pro and Max (or behind a company gateway). Even with the collector installed, those cards may stay at "Waiting for data".

content.text:
Both Claude problems are explained and fixed where they could be, and all the requested changes are in. Checks, both builds and all 94 tests pass, and I reviewed each screen in the browser. The preview at http://127.0.0.1:4174/ is serving the new build; reload to see it. Nothing is committed.

**Why Claude Code (default) said "Partial data":** Claude Code only reported its 5-hour window, with no weekly one. Claude's docs say a window can be missing (it isn't sent yet, or it was dropped after a reset), but the dashboard treated a missing window as a partial read. That was a bug. The card now shows "Up to date"; a window with bad values still counts as partial.

**Why Serro isn't working:** the collector was installed correctly and works: I ran it by hand and it passed the config-directory check. But the only Serro session (PID 13090) started at 15:25, before the collector was installed at 15:27. No snapshot has ever arrived, which most likely means Claude Code reads its status-line setting only when a session starts. That's an inference I couldn't confirm. **Restart that Serro Claude Code session and send a message.** To make this visible, each collector run now records when it ran and what happened. Cards then say one of:
- "Collector installed but hasn't run yet. Restart sessions opened before that" (Serro's current state)
- the collector ran but Claude Code sent no quota
- the collector ran from the wrong config directory

**What's new:**
- **Settings page:** new Usage and Settings tabs in the top bar. Settings has:
  - **Percentage display:** Used or Remaining. This switches every value, meter, trend chart and the summary card ("Highest usage" becomes "Lowest remaining").
  - **Auto-refresh:** moved here from the top bar.
  - **Accounts list:** with a Manage button per account.
  - **Clear history** button.
- **Equal card heights:** cards in a row now match, the footer sits at the bottom, and the waiting message is shorter.
- **Footer:** "Observed …" is gone. It shows only the last refreshed time, with the source and age in a tooltip.
- **Resets dialog:** clicking "Resets in …" or "N banked resets" opens it. It shows the exact reset time, window length and start, time elapsed, used and remaining, the pace estimate, and banked resets with their earliest expiry. The window you clicked is highlighted.
- **Email:** read from Codex and from `claude auth status`, shown under the plan (for example `dev@21n.co`, `Aravind@serro.ai`). It's hidden when the account name already is the email. It's kept out of the agent text output and out of history.
- **Weekly Fable limit:** Claude Code's docs only list a 5-hour, weekly and spend window for the status line. The installed CLI does use model-specific weekly keys internally (`seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`), but there's no Fable key and nothing documents them reaching the status line. So the collector now keeps `seven_day_fable`, `_opus`, `_sonnet` and `_haiku` and shows them as "Weekly Fable usage" and so on, but only if Claude Code ever sends them. Right now it doesn't.
- **Layout:** each window is now a title-and-value row with a full-width meter underneath, so names like "Weekly usage" are no longer cut off.

I also made one older test less timing-sensitive; it was failing occasionally on a busy machine. Dark mode is still unchecked.

<result>I found no documented, read-only way to get a Factory Droid account's remaining subscription quota. Droid's status line and hooks carry no quota or rate-limit fields, there is no `droid usage` command, and the public APIs that touch usage are org-admin or Enterprise-only. Synara is the one product I checked that shows Droid quota, and it does so by decrypting Droid's stored login and calling an undocumented Factory endpoint.

## 1. What Factory documents
Docs are at docs.factory.com; docs.factory.ai redirects there.

**Status line**
- Setting `statusLine` in `~/.factory/settings.json` takes `{ "command": string, "padding"?: number, "maxRows"?: number }` and is configured with `/statusline` ([settings](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/settings.md)).
- The docs don't list the JSON sent to the command on stdin. From the local binary, the fields are `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `session_settings_path`, `cwd`, `workspace.current_dir`, `model{id, display_name, reasoning_effort}`, `context{last_call_compaction_tokens, token_limit, adjusted_tokens, adjusted_limit, percentage, display}` and `version`.
- That is context-window use only, not quota. This differs from Claude Code, whose status line now receives `rate_limits`.

**Hooks**
- Every hook payload carries `session_id`, `transcript_path`, `cwd`, `permission_mode`, `hook_event_name` and optionally `message_id` ([hooks](https://docs.factory.com/harness/hooks.md)).
- None carries token, credit or quota data. The closest are `PreCompact.estimated_tokens` and `SessionEnd.session_duration_ms`.

**CLI**
- The slash commands are interactive only, with no `--json` output ([CLI reference](https://docs.factory.com/droid-cli/cli-reference.md)):
  - `/cost`: usage for the current session
  - `/stats [period]`: usage statistics
  - `/limits`: credit rate limits and overage preferences
  - `/billing`: billing settings
  - `/context`: context-window breakdown
- There is no `droid usage` subcommand. `droid exec -o json` and `droid doctor --json` exist but say nothing about quota.

**API** (base `https://api.factory.ai`, header `Authorization: Bearer fk-…`)
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/tokens` and `/users` are organization-wide and need the Manager or Owner role ([analytics](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/analytics.md)).
- `GET /api/v1/analytics/cost/me/query` returns only the caller's own data, but only for "Enterprise organizations with Analytics enabled."
- `GET/PUT /api/v0/organization/usage/limits/{global,users}` read and set per-user credit caps set by an admin ([organization](https://docs.factory.com/api-reference/organization.md)). Response fields are not documented.
- No documented endpoint returns personal remaining quota, rolling-window percentage or reset time.
- API keys come from the org's API Keys settings, mainly for service accounts, which run as their own principal rather than as you ([identity and access](https://docs.factory.com/enterprise/identity-and-access.md)).

**Running several accounts**
- Documented: `FACTORY_API_KEY`, set per process.
- Undocumented, found in the binary: `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE`, which replaces the home directory so Droid uses `<override>/.factory`. Note that the keychain item that holds the credential encryption key (service `"Factory CLI"`, account `auth-encryption-key`) is the same for every home.

**Plan and limit concepts** ([individual pricing](https://docs.factory.com/pricing/individuals.md))
- Plans: Pro $20/mo, Plus $100/mo (about 5× Pro usage), Max $200/mo (about 10×).
- Rate limits run in three independent rolling windows: 5-hour, 7-day and 30-day. Each starts at first use and resets after it elapses.
- Standard Usage is spent first and does not carry over month to month.
- Droid Core is a free open-weight model pool with its own rate limits, used after Standard Usage runs out.
- Extra Usage is prepaid USD credit ($10 minimum) that does not expire.
- The pricing page does not describe the allowance as tokens per month. A separate profile preference sends emails at 80% and 100% of the "monthly credit cap."

## 2. How the other products do it

**Synara** (MIT, [Emanuele-web04/synara](https://github.com/Emanuele-web04/synara)) does show Droid quota, in `apps/server/src/providerUsage/providers/droid.ts` and `droidCredentials.ts`:
- It decrypts `~/.factory/auth.v2.{loginkeychain,keyring,file}` with AES-256-GCM. The key comes from `/usr/bin/security` (service `"Factory CLI"`, account `auth-encryption-key-security-cli` or `auth-encryption-key`) or from `~/.factory/auth.v2.key`.
- It then calls the undocumented `GET https://api.factory.ai/api/billing/limits` (`api.eu.factory.ai` for EU) with `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>` and `X-Factory-Org-Id`. If `FACTORY_API_KEY` is set, it first calls the undocumented `/api/cli/whoami` with `X-Factory-Whoami-Extended: true`.
- Fields it parses:
  - `limits.standard.{fiveHour,weekly,monthly}.{usedPercent,windowEnd}`
  - `limits.core.*`
  - `extraUsageBalanceCents`
  - `overagePreference`
  - `usesTokenRateLimitsBilling`
- The installed droid binary uses the same endpoint behind `/limits`; it also references `extraUsageAllowed` and `canManageOverage`.
- For multiple accounts it relies on a separate home directory or environment (`*_HOME`) per configured account, or `FACTORY_API_KEY`. Each result is keyed by home directory and a credential fingerprint.
- For Claude and Codex it calls `api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` and `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`, both undocumented.

**Orca** ([stablyai/orca](https://github.com/stablyai/orca)) does not track Droid usage. Its [usage-tracking docs](https://www.onorca.dev/docs/agents/usage-tracking) don't list Droid.
- `~/.orca/agent-hooks/droid-hook.sh` only forwards Droid hook events (Notification, PermissionRequest and so on) to `http://127.0.0.1:$ORCA_AGENT_HOOK_PORT/hook/droid`. If that fails, it writes them to a local spool file.
- `claude-statusline.sh` passes along Claude's documented status-line payload when it contains `rate_limits`, posting it with `configDir=$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` to `/statusline/claude` at most once every 15 seconds.
- Orca also reads Claude's `.credentials.json` or keychain entry and calls `/api/oauth/usage`. For Codex it uses an RPC rate-limit probe plus `wham/usage`.
- It has an account switcher for Claude, Codex and others.

**Zeron** ([zeronsh/zeron](https://github.com/zeronsh/zeron)) has no Droid support. In `crates/engine/src/agent_accounts.rs` it reads Claude's `.credentials.json` under `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and Codex's `auth.json` under `CODEX_HOME`, then calls `api/oauth/usage` and `wham/usage`.

## 3. Local droid CLI
- `/opt/homebrew/bin/droid` reports version 0.236.0; it sits in the Homebrew cask folder labelled 0.74.0.
- Subcommands: `exec`, `daemon`, `search`, `update`, `mcp`, `plugin`, `computer` and `doctor` (`--json`, `--auth`). There is no usage or limits subcommand.
- `~/.factory/settings.json` has no `statusLine`. Its `hooks` already run Orca's `droid-hook.sh` and a Superset `notify.sh`.
- The login store exists as `~/.factory/auth.v2.loginkeychain`, `auth.v2.file`, `auth.v2.key` and `auth.encrypted`. I did not read any of them.

## Recommendation
- **Most legitimate documented source:** none gives personal remaining quota.
  - For Enterprise orgs, `GET /api/v1/analytics/cost/me/query` with the user's own `fk-` key returns only that user's spend.
  - Org Managers can read `organization/usage/limits/*`. Those are admin-set caps, not live quota.
  - The account boundary is the API key's principal and org. That means one key per account, kept in the OS credential store and supplied by the user.
- **Otherwise:** show Droid quota as "unavailable." The fallback is to send users to the `/limits` view or `app.factory.ai/settings/usage`. Hooks and the status line can add per-session context use, labelled as a local measurement.
- **Flag – reading another tool's stored login:** decrypting `~/.factory/auth.v2.*` with the "Factory CLI" keychain key, as Synara does, reads Droid's stored tokens. It breaks AGENTS.md's approved-credential rule.
- **Flag – undocumented endpoints:** `/api/billing/limits` and `/api/cli/whoami` are internal Droid calls. Calling them would need Factory's explicit approval.
- **Same flags for Claude and Codex:** `api/oauth/usage` and `wham/usage` are undocumented and need those tools' stored tokens. Claude's status-line `rate_limits`, which is documented and applies per `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, is the clean option there.
- **Unofficial multi-account isolation:** `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE` is undocumented.

Everything you asked for is built, including Factory Droid with multiple accounts. The new **Use local sign-ins** switch is in Settings, off by default; I haven't turned it on. All 103 tests, the checks and both builds pass. I checked the screens in the browser in light and dark mode, and the preview at http://127.0.0.1:4174/ is serving the new build. Nothing is committed.

**UI changes**
- **Bar colours:** each meter is now one colour for that window's state: green under 60% used, amber under 85%, red above. That also fixes Remaining mode, which was showing the whole colour range.
- **Provider logos:** Iconify's CC0 `logos` set for Codex, Claude, Cursor and Antigravity. A generator script, `scripts/generate-provider-logos.mjs`, copies just those icons into the package, so the full icon set isn't bundled. The OpenAI and Cursor logos follow the text colour so they show in dark mode. Iconify has no Factory logo, so Droid uses a Phosphor robot icon.
- **Filter row:** All / Codex / Claude Code / … chips with counts above the cards. The summary cards follow the filter.
- **Dropdown:** the auto-refresh dropdown is back in the top bar with a padded chevron.
- **Cards:** the logo is aligned to the top of the heading, and the footer no longer shows the source ("Codex app-server", "snapshot").
- **Theme:** System / Light / Dark in Settings; the trend chart redraws when it changes.

**How the others do it**

All three read the CLIs' stored sign-ins and call undocumented endpoints. None uses a documented source for quota.
- **Synara:** decrypts Droid's stored login with its key from the macOS keychain, reads Claude's token from the keychain or credentials file, and reads Codex's token file.
- **Orca:** collects Claude's status line, reads Claude's stored token, and doesn't track Droid.
- **Zeron:** reads Claude's and Codex's credential files, and doesn't track Droid.

**What the new switch does**
- **Off (default):** a Droid account needs a Factory API key. You set the key in the usage server's environment and give Subset only the variable name, as with Cursor. Claude keeps using the collector.
- **On, Factory Droid:** Subset decrypts the Droid sign-in stored in each account's Factory home, then reads the 5-hour, weekly and monthly limits (standard and Core) plus the extra-usage balance. For a second account, start Droid with `FACTORY_HOME_OVERRIDE=<dir> droid`; account settings show this command.
- **On, Claude Code:** Subset first runs `claude auth status`, which lets Claude Code refresh its own token. It then reads the stored token for that config directory and gets live usage, including **Weekly Fable** if your account has it. That limit is in the usage response, not the status line, which is why the collector never got it. Live reads don't depend on the collector, so Serro should show data without restarting its session.
- **On, Codex:** unchanged. Codex app-server already reads Codex's own sign-in through a supported interface.

**Safety limits**
- Read-only: tokens are never refreshed, written, stored, logged or sent to the page.
- Subset never uses Claude's refresh token. Anthropic issues a new one on each use, so using it from Subset would sign Claude Code out.

**What to know before turning it on**
- **Keychain prompt:** macOS will probably ask to allow keychain access the first time. Choose **Always Allow**, or each auto-refresh will wait on the prompt.
- **Undocumented endpoints:** Factory and Anthropic don't document the usage endpoints, so either can change or stop working without notice. The UI and README say so.
- **Repo rule:** this is an exception to the AGENTS.md rule against reading other tools' credentials. I recorded it in AGENTS.md as your 2026-10-08 decision, limited to this off-by-default setting.
- **Untested against the real services:** the code is tested only with fake credentials and responses. Real Claude and Factory responses may differ from Synara's code, which is what I based the parsing on. If something looks off after you turn it on, tell me what the cards show.
- **macOS only:** keychain reading is macOS-only. Elsewhere only credential files are read.

All ten changes are in. While checking them I found a new problem: Anthropic is rate-limiting Subset's live Claude checks. I added backoff, but the two Claude cards will show that warning until Anthropic lifts the limit. Checks, both builds and all 104 tests pass, and the preview is running the new build. Nothing is committed.

**What changed:**
1. **Default tag:** the default Codex and Claude sign-ins show a neutral "Default" tag beside the name.
2. **Status pills:** "Up to date" is no longer shown. Other statuses (Waiting for data, Partial data, Stale, Signed out) appear at the left of the card footer.
3. **Optional names:** an unnamed account shows its email, then "<Provider> account". The two default accounts dropped their old names, so they now show `samalaaravind02@gmail.com` and `dev@21n.co`. Long names are cut off with "…" and shown in full on hover.
4. **Trend charts setting:** a new switch in Settings, on by default.
5. **Filter chips:** they show just the logo, with no circle behind it.
6. **Layout shift:** it came from the scrollbar appearing or disappearing between the long dashboard and the shorter settings page. The page now always reserves room for the scrollbar, and the top bar measures at the same position on both pages.
7. **Auto-refresh dropdown:** removed from the top bar; the setting stays in Settings.
8. **Tab name:** "Usage" is now "Dashboard".
9. **Refresh button:** icon only, with a tooltip and the `R` shortcut.
10. **Local sign-ins:** on by default, and you can turn them off in Settings. The AGENTS.md exception and the README now say "on by default at the owner's request".

**Live data works:** the first real read gave dev@21n.co 5-hour 20% and **Weekly Fable 19%**, and Serro 5-hour 4% and weekly 44%. No keychain prompt appeared. The Serro card no longer depends on its collector.

**The rate limit:** my repeated test requests plus page loads hit Anthropic's limit on its usage endpoint, which is what the cards in your screenshot show. Live reads now:
- happen at most every 2 minutes per Claude account and every minute per Factory account;
- after a rate limit, keep showing the last good values and wait for the provider's `Retry-After` header (or 5 minutes) before calling again.

content.text:
All ten items are done: Codex resets can now be used from the dashboard, and Amp, Devin, Pi and OpenCode are supported. All 111 tests, the checks and both builds pass. I checked the loading screen, the sticky header, the resets dialog and closing dialogs by clicking outside in the browser. The preview is running the new build. Nothing is committed, and I haven't used a reset.

**Your questions**
- **5. Why the rate limit:** Anthropic's usage endpoint allows only a few requests per sign-in. Three things used it up:
  - Subset had no throttle at first, and my test requests made several calls within a minute.
  - Every page load and auto-refresh called it again.
  - Orca, per its docs, polls the same endpoint with the same Claude sign-in, so the two apps likely share one limit.

  Subset now reads each Claude account live at most every 5 minutes. After a rate limit it keeps the last good values and waits for Anthropic's `Retry-After` header (or 5 minutes) before trying again.
- **6. Factory logo:** Iconify has no Factory logo. Factory's own `factory.ai/favicon.svg` is now included (a plain SVG, no scripts) and follows the text colour.
- **8. "≈" in remaining mode:** you're right; remaining is just 100% minus usage. "≈" now marks only real estimates such as pace.
- **10. Factory "partial":** Factory leaves out the end time for a window that hasn't started. That was treated as missing data; it now shows "Starts on first use" and isn't marked partial.
- **10. Antigravity no data:** the collector is installed correctly, but the only `agy` session running started on Oct 2, before installation, and sessions only pick up the collector when they start. Start a new `agy` session.

**What changed**
1. **Codex resets:**
   - The resets dialog lists each banked reset with its title, description, and grant and expiry dates (yours: two "Full reset" credits).
   - **Use a reset…** asks for confirmation, then calls Codex's own `account/rateLimitResetCredit/consume`. Codex picks the credit.
   - It reports the outcome and refreshes.
   - It's the only action in the dashboard that changes anything at a provider.
2. **New providers:**
   - **Amp:** uses its official `amp usage` command for the credit balance and today's Amp Free allowance. Another account can be added by naming an environment variable holding its API key.
   - **Devin:** reads daily and weekly quota with the key `devin auth login` stored, or a named API key variable. It only contacts https servers on codeium.com, windsurf.com or devin.ai.
   - **Pi and OpenCode:** you choose a stored login, and the card shows the quota of the ChatGPT, Claude or OpenCode Go subscription behind it. On this Mac, Pi has ChatGPT and Claude logins and OpenCode has ChatGPT. Subset only reads those tokens; Pi and OpenCode refresh them.
   - **Endpoints:** Devin, ChatGPT and OpenCode Go use endpoints their makers don't document, so they can change without notice.
3. **Loading:** the first load shows placeholder cards instead of "No accounts yet".
4. **Header:** stays at the top while scrolling.
5. **Plans:**
   - Codex `prolite` and `promax` now show as "Pro Lite" and "Pro Max".
   - Claude live reads show tiers like "Max 5x" or "Max 20x"; yours show "Team".
   - Codex doesn't report dollar tiers, so I didn't invent $100/$200/$500 labels.
6. **Dialogs:** clicking outside closes them.

**Not checked live:**
- The new providers aren't added to your dashboard, so I haven't seen them against the real services. Their tests use fake CLIs and responses.
- Your Devin `credentials.toml` exists but wasn't used.
- Live Antigravity reads would need Google OAuth token refreshes (Synara's approach), which I didn't add.

content.text:
All nine are done, including personal Cursor usage from the Cursor app sign-in. All 116 tests, the checks and both builds pass, and I checked the dashboard, resets dialog, sort menu, pins and add dialog in the browser. The preview is running the new build. Nothing is committed, and no reset was used.

1. **"≈" is gone everywhere.** The footnote now says that usage, limits and resets are provider-reported, and that pace, run-out times, window start and credit dollar values are estimates.
2. **Resets dialog is simpler:**
   - Each window shows Resets, Window started, "33% used · 67% left" and "At this pace". The window-length and time-elapsed rows are gone.
   - The repeated "Thanks for using Codex!" text is removed; each credit shows its title, grant date and expiry.
   - The credit that will be used is tagged "Used next", and the text under the button names it with its expiry date.
   - Subset now asks Codex for that exact credit (the one expiring first) instead of letting Codex pick, so the dialog and the action always match.
3. **"Max 5x" was wrong because** Claude stores your seat's rate tier as `default_claude_max_5x` even though the subscription is Team. The label now uses the subscription type first, so it reads **Team Premium 5x**.
4. **Paid credits:**
   - Codex shows "60,385.15 credits", with "about $2,415.41 at list price" underneath ($40 per 1,000 credits, the same estimate Synara uses).
   - Claude shows "Extra usage" with its monthly limit: Serro has $0.00 used of $10.
   - Factory's extra-usage balance and Cursor's credit grants also show where available.
5. **Cursor:** yes, it can. There's a new **Cursor** account type (separate from Cursor team). It reads the Cursor app's sign-in from the keychain, falling back to Cursor's local database read-only, and calls the usage endpoints Cursor's own settings page uses. Cursor doesn't document them. A live test read your Pro plan at 66.4% used with a reset date. Add it from **Add account → Cursor** to see it on the dashboard.
6. **Radio buttons** now line up with their labels. The account-name field's input styling was also being applied to radio buttons.
7. **Pinning:** each card has a pin button. Pinned cards get a **Pinned** chip right after All.
8. **Sort:** an icon-only button at the end of the filter row offers Default order, Recently used first and Expiring first.
   - "Recently used" uses the latest time an account's usage went up in local history.
   - "Expiring" uses the soonest reset.
   - Pins and sort order are saved per browser. I cleared the ones my test clicks left in the browser I used for checking.
9. **Trend chart:** resets show as dashed "Reset" lines where usage dropped sharply. Your dev@21n.co chart already shows one.

The Antigravity collector has now run, but Antigravity's status line sent no quota fields, so that card stays empty. That seems to depend on the Antigravity plan. Showing it would need Synara's approach of refreshing Google OAuth tokens, which I haven't added.

content.text:
All six are done, and I checked them in the browser on the running preview. All 117 tests, the checks and both builds pass. Nothing is committed.

1. **Pin is in the card's ⋯ menu** (Pin / Unpin and Account settings). A pinned card shows a pin icon in its footer, and the menu closes when you click outside it or press Escape.
2. **Cursor shows its full breakdown.** Cursor's response splits usage into Total (66.4%), **Auto + Composer** (68.1%) and **API models** (57.7%), and the card now shows all three. It also shows:
   - included usage ($20 of $20)
   - bonus usage ($146.03, beyond included usage at no charge)
   - team pooled spend ($4,457.49)
   - on-demand spend and credit grants, when Cursor reports them
   - the plan name ("Team"), from Cursor's plan endpoint

   There's no Grok or bot split in what Cursor returns for your account, so I couldn't add one.
3. **Credits** now sit at the bottom of the card, just above the footer. The note ("about $2,415.41 at list price") is on its own line under the label, so the run-together spacing is fixed.
4. **Amp card:** the spacing is fixed, and the empty "No usage windows reported" line no longer shows for accounts that only have balances.
   - **Amp logo:** the old one was Google's AMP logo, which shares the name. It's now Amp's own app icon from `ampcode.com/app-icon.svg`, filling the tile.
   - **Pi logo:** it's now the mark from `pi.dev/favicon.svg`, recolored to work in both themes.

   Both are plain SVGs vendored in `scripts/logos`.
5. **Claude Extra usage** is at the bottom of the card, with the meter full width and "Limit $10.00" underneath.
6. **Provider filter chips** stay on one line and scroll sideways with a visible scrollbar. The sort button stays fixed at the right.

1. scrollbar shouldn't be visible for filter chips row
2. Make credits, extra usage data optional like trends in settings
3. change the sort button as options button and then Show the trends, credits data toggles in the popover along side sort option
4. For Factory card - instead of rendering both Core, normal usage all at once - render a tab switcher and render separately to avoid long height of that one card
5. Add support for https://omp.sh/ and hermes agent similar to pi, opencode if that's straitforward
6. In the top row cards - show provider name as well for next reset, lowest remaining etc
7. In the top row accounts card - show split of providers visually using pie chart (dont include harnesses like pi, opencode etc - group by sub accounts like codex, claude etc)
8. In the provider filters - dont render harnesses like Open code, Pi, Omp etc (that has sub accounts) - render sub accounts like pi + Codex etc in codex, claude etc retaining the current card information (which shows the harness logo etc)

Here's the plan for all eight:

1. **Filter chips:** hide the scrollbar on the row.
2. **Credits setting:** make credits and extra usage optional, like trends.
3. **Options button:** replace the sort button with an options button holding the sort choices plus the trends and credits toggles.
4. **Factory card:** add a Standard / Core tab switcher.
5. **omp and Hermes:** research them, then add them like Pi and OpenCode if they're simple.
6. **Summary cards:** show the provider name.
7. **Accounts pie chart:** split accounts by underlying service (Codex, Claude, and so on), not by harness.
8. **Grouping by service:** file harness accounts (Pi, OpenCode, …) under the service their login belongs to.

what does it take for us to distribute usage as a downloadable macOS app or run via CLI as localhost?

**Short answer:** a localhost CLI is about 1–2 days of packaging work. A downloadable macOS app is about 1–2 weeks, most of it Apple signing, notarization and auto-update rather than features. I'd ship the CLI first, then wrap the same UI in a menu-bar app.

## What both need first
- **Stable collector path:** installed Claude and Antigravity collectors run `node /Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/subset/apps/usage/server.mjs collect …`, so they break once the app lives somewhere else. Installed builds need a fixed command (`subset-usage collect …` on PATH, or a shim at `~/.local/share/subset/bin`), plus a migration that rewrites already-installed collectors.
- **Self-contained build:** the host imports the private `@subset/usage` workspace and serves `apps/usage/dist`. Bundle the server, packages and built UI into one artifact.
- **Local API protection:** the server binds to `127.0.0.1` and checks Origin, but any local process can still call it without an Origin header. That includes reading usage, installing collectors and using a Codex reset. A per-launch secret token is worth adding before strangers run it.
- **Local sign-ins default:** "Use local sign-ins" is on by default by your choice, and it reads other tools' credentials and calls undocumented endpoints (Claude, Factory, ChatGPT `wham`, Cursor, Devin). For a public release I'd ask for consent on first run instead of defaulting to on.
- **Repo rules (AGENTS.md):**
  - npm packages must use the `@sub-set/` scope.
  - Nothing gets published, and no download link goes up, until the artifact is verified.
  - The catalog's `availableSurfaces` is updated only after a release check.
  - The Superfunctions reuse rule means checking `clifn` (for the CLI) and `hostfn` before building your own.

## CLI on localhost (`npx @sub-set/usage`)
1. **Package:** publish `@sub-set/usage` with a `subset-usage` command: `serve` (default), `status --json`, `collect`, plus `--port` and `--no-open`.
2. **Bundle:** one bundle (esbuild or tsup) containing the server, the `@subset/usage` code and the built UI. Requires Node ≥ 22 or a `bun build --compile` binary.
3. **On start:** pick a free port, open the browser, and shut down cleanly on Ctrl-C. Optionally add a `subset-usage install-agent` command that runs it at login.
4. **Release:** a versioned publish from CI, a smoke test of the published package on a clean machine, then update the catalog.

The UI, data storage and readers already work as they are.

## Downloadable macOS app
**Recommended route:** Tauri v2 (a small native shell around WebKit) or Electron, wrapping the existing Svelte UI. The server runs alongside it as a compiled binary (Tauri), or inside the app itself (Electron, which ships Node). That's no UI rewrite. A native SwiftUI menu-bar app would mean rewriting the UI.

What you need:
- **Distribution:** a Developer ID download, not the Mac App Store. The App Store requires sandboxing, which blocks reading `~/.codex`, `~/.claude`, other apps' keychain items, and running `codex`, `claude` or `amp`.
- **Apple Developer account:** $99 a year, for a Developer ID Application certificate, hardened runtime, notarization (`notarytool`) and stapling, packaged as a DMG.
- **Auto-update:** Sparkle, or Tauri's updater with a signed update feed, hosted on GitHub Releases or R2, with published checksums.
- **PATH handling:** apps opened from Finder get a minimal PATH and won't find `codex`, `claude` or `amp`. You'd resolve the login shell's PATH or let users set binary locations.
- **Keychain prompts:** they'll come from the app instead of `/usr/bin/security`, so users answer them once per item, and again after an update if the signature changes.
- **What an app adds:** a menu-bar icon with the lowest remaining percentage, launch at login, notifications when an account runs low or resets, and background refresh without a browser tab.
- **Rough effort:** 3–5 days for a working app, about 1 day for signing and notarization setup, and about 1 day for auto-update and the release pipeline.

## Recommendation
1. **Now:** fix the collector path, add the local API token, and put local sign-ins behind a first-run consent screen. These are needed either way.
2. **Next:** publish the `@sub-set/usage` CLI. It's the fastest real release, and it proves the bundling.
3. **Then:** build a Tauri menu-bar app around the same bundle, distributed as a signed, notarized DMG.

on:

# Subset

Subset is a collection of small, independently useful apps. Each app solves one focused problem and can, where its platform allows, also serve as a capability inside 21n products or as an interface returned by an AI agent.

The first pilots are a **usage dashboard** and a **PDF annotation and review tool**. The local usage preview supports isolated Codex/ChatGPT connections, separately collected Claude Code and Antigravity CLI quota snapshots, and authorized Cursor team-member spending reports. Personal Cursor subscription quota is not supported; neither pilot is released. The directory labels availability accordingly.

## Product model

A Subset capability has a clear user outcome, its own data and operations, and one or more delivery surfaces:

| Surface | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Standalone web app | A usage dashboard opened from the Subset directory |
| Embedded web view | The same usage view inside Nucleum or Outright |
| Agent interface | A trusted, registered view shown beside a structured tool result |
14:| Agent delivery | Structured result, optional registered view; separate local CLI/skill | Planned. Each host and the published CLI/skill require their own verification. |
16:The usage dashboard boundary is normalized per-source status and explicit read operations. Its sources are ChatGPT-signed-in Codex homes through the documented local app-server protocol, independently collected Claude Code/Antigravity CLI quota snapshots, and authorized Cursor team-member spending through its official Admin API. Quota snapshots and spending caps remain distinct; personal Cursor subscriptions and API billing are not implemented quota sources. The standalone host owns profile persistence and collector bindings, while the package owns normalization and source reads. Proposed consumers are a standalone web host, an Outright adapter, a local CLI and skill for shell-capable agents, and a registered view in an agent host. The PDF review boundary is document identity, page/annotation operations, and explicit export; web, native, product, and agent views may differ. No capability may import an app or a consuming product.
