## Local sign-ins (opt-in)

**Settings → Use local sign-ins** is on by default (the repository owner's choice) and stored server-side in `usage-preferences.json`; turning it off stops all reads of stored sign-ins. When on:

- **Claude Code:** for each account bound to a config directory, the host first runs `claude auth status` (Claude Code refreshes its own token there), then reads the stored OAuth access token from the macOS keychain item `Claude Code-credentials` (default directory) or `Claude Code-credentials-<first 8 hex of SHA-256 of the directory>`, falling back to `<dir>/.credentials.json`. It calls `https://api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage` read-only and shows `five_hour`, `seven_day`, and `limits[]` entries of kind `weekly_scoped` (per-model weekly limits such as Fable). Subset never calls the token endpoint: Anthropic rotates refresh tokens, so refreshing would sign Claude Code out. An expired token asks the user to open Claude Code. If no stored sign-in is found, the status-line snapshot is used.
- **Factory Droid:** reads `<factory home>/.factory/auth.v2.loginkeychain`, `auth.v2.keyring`, or `auth.v2.file`, decrypts it (AES-256-GCM) with the key from the keychain item `Factory CLI` or `auth.v2.key`, and calls `https://api.factory.ai/api/billing/limits` (or the EU host) with the account's organization. When off, a Droid account needs a Factory API key variable; Subset then calls `/api/cli/whoami` for the organization and the same limits endpoint.
- **Codex** is unchanged: Codex app-server already reads its own sign-in through a documented interface.

Neither endpoint is documented by its provider, so either can change or stop working. Tokens stay in memory for one request and are never stored, logged, or sent to the view. macOS may show a keychain prompt the first time; choose **Always Allow** so auto-refresh does not wait on it. The approach follows Synara (MIT; `apps/server/src/providerUsage/providers`), Orca, and Zeron, which read the same stores. Subset's implementation is independent and read-only. Keychain lookup is macOS-only; elsewhere only credential files are read.

## Standalone local preview

In the local dashboard, choose **Use current Codex account** to add the existing ChatGPT sign-in, then enter a label and choose **Connect another ChatGPT account**. The host starts the [documented Codex app-server browser login](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/app-server) in a new, isolated Codex home. Follow **Continue with ChatGPT** and choose the intended account in the browser. The dashboard polls the login result and adds the account after Codex confirms a ChatGPT sign-in. A browser reload recovers the active sign-in ID, validated link, and state from the same local server, restoring progress and cancellation controls without persisting credentials or login state in browser storage. This recovery does not survive a server restart. Subset never sees or stores OAuth tokens; Codex manages them in its own home. **Remove** unlinks an existing Codex home from the dashboard; for a Subset-managed home it also deletes that local sign-in after explicit confirmation. Cancelling an unfinished login deletes only its newly created home.

The host stores profile labels and Codex home paths in `~/.config/subset/codex-profiles.json` with owner-only file permissions. Managed Codex homes live under `~/.local/share/subset/codex-accounts/`, each with owner-only directory permissions. An owner-controlled profile file may also be supplied directly, for example:

```json
[
  { "id": "personal", "label": "Personal", "codexHome": "/absolute/path/to/personal-codex-home" },
  { "id": "work", "label": "Work", "codexHome": "/absolute/path/to/work-codex-home" }
]
```

Each manually added home must already be signed in with its intended ChatGPT account using Codex. `CODEX_HOME=/absolute/path/to/personal-codex-home codex login` is the Codex-managed login path. `--profile` selects a config overlay within one home and is not account isolation. Do not copy auth files between homes. Account email is not stored in profile metadata or sent to the dashboard status view, so labels should distinguish accounts. A second real ChatGPT sign-in has not yet been available for live two-account verification.

After `npm run build`, use `npm run status --workspace=@subset/usage-web` for structured JSON or `npm run serve --workspace=@subset/usage-web` for the local view at `http://127.0.0.1:4174`. `SUBSET_USAGE_PROFILES_FILE` selects a different JSON file; the existing `SUBSET_CODEX_PROFILES_FILE` remains a fallback for persisted Codex setups. The default stays `~/.config/subset/codex-profiles.json` and accepts all provider types. `SUBSET_USAGE_DATA_DIR` optionally selects a managed data directory; `SUBSET_USAGE_PORT` changes the loopback port. Stop the server with Ctrl-C or SIGTERM. The server binds only to `127.0.0.1`, checks Host and Origin headers, and requires a matching browser Origin for account mutations. This is a local preview, not a published CLI/skill, hosted agent view, or public web app. OpenAI documents Codex app-server authentication for local or open-source applications, with a different authorization path required for commercial or hosted services.

## Claude and Antigravity collectors

In **Manage accounts**, choose **Claude Code quota snapshot** or **Antigravity CLI quota snapshot**, give the account a distinct label, and choose **Add snapshot account**. Expand that account's collector setup and use its generated command, which includes its unique local ID and any custom profile file selection. The command reads JSON on stdin, writes an owner-only quota snapshot, and deliberately produces no stdout.

**Automatic installation.** For a Claude Code account bound to a config directory, or an Antigravity account, **Install collector** (on the card, in account settings, or as a checkbox when adding the account) writes the collector into that CLI's `settings.json`. It is an explicit operation: Subset first copies the file to `settings.json.subset-backup`, keeps every other key, and saves the replaced `statusLine` in an owner-only Subset file. The collector then runs that previous status line with the same input, so an existing display (for example Orca's) keeps rendering. **Uninstall** or removing the account restores the previous `statusLine` unless another tool has since replaced it. Status-line collectors only run in CLI sessions started after installation; a session that was already open keeps its old settings. Account settings report whether the collector is installed, missing, or replaced by another tool. Each collector run records only its time and outcome (`saved`, `no-quota`, or `wrong-directory`) in an owner-only `collector-runs` directory, so the dashboard can say whether the collector has not run yet (for example, a CLI session opened before installation), ran without quota, or ran from the wrong config directory. Settings that are not valid JSON are never rewritten. An account without a config directory cannot be installed automatically.

For manual setup, configure that command as `statusLine.command` in the intended Claude Code account environment or Antigravity CLI's `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`. For example, using the absolute host path and generated account ID:

```json
{
  "statusLine": {
    "type": "command",
    "command": "node /absolute/path/to/subset/apps/usage/server.mjs collect --account claude_example"
  }
}
```

The default Claude Code account (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, or `~/.claude` when unset) appears automatically as **Claude Code (default)** when the documented `claude auth status --json` command reports it signed in. Each refresh runs that command for every Claude account with a config directory to show its sign-in state and plan; Subset strips token variables from its environment, keeps only `loggedIn`, `authMethod`, `subscriptionType`, and `configDirectory`, and skips directories that do not exist because the CLI would create them. Removing the default account is remembered in `usage-preferences.json` next to the profile file; **Use default Claude Code account** adds it back. Quota still comes only from the status-line collector.

For several Claude Code accounts, use one [`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/env-vars) per account (for example `~/.claude` and `~/.claude-work`, launched with `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude`) and enter that directory when adding the account. The host stores it as `claudeConfigDir`, requires it to be unique, and shows the launch command, the `settings.json` path, and the `statusLine` JSON for that account. The collector rejects a payload whose `transcript_path` lies under a different `<config dir>/projects/` tree, falling back to `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` in its environment when no transcript path is present. Claude Code's subprocess env scrub can remove `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so a payload with neither signal is accepted. An account without a config directory keeps the unchecked binding. The transcript path is used only for this check and is never stored.

Use the generated command verbatim when paths contain spaces. This collector alone renders no status-line text. To retain an existing status line, use a wrapper that passes the same stdin JSON to the collector and existing renderer, without logging or persisting the raw payload. Subset edits provider settings only through the explicit install and uninstall operations above.

The [Claude Code status-line contract](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline#rate-limit-usage) supplies `rate_limits.five_hour` and `rate_limits.seven_day`, with `used_percentage` and epoch-second `resets_at`. These subscription fields are documented for Pro/Max after the first API response. Claude Code omits a window it has no data for and drops one after it resets, so an absent window is not reported as partial data; a present window with invalid values is. The installed Claude Code CLI uses model-scoped weekly keys such as `seven_day_opus` internally, but they are not documented for the status line. The collector keeps `seven_day_fable`, `seven_day_opus`, `seven_day_sonnet`, and `seven_day_haiku` only if the status-line JSON includes them, shown as for example "Weekly Fable usage". Remaining quota is calculated from reported usage, not inferred from tokens or context size.

The [Antigravity CLI status-line contract](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/statusline/) supplies `quota.<bucket>.remaining_fraction`, `reset_time`, optional `reset_in_seconds`, and optional `plan_tier`. Remaining quota is reported, while used percentage is calculated. A countdown reset is anchored to the capture time, not the dashboard refresh time.

Snapshots store only allowlisted quota fields and optional plan tier. Emails, transcripts, credentials, workspace paths, and other CLI metadata are discarded. Stored envelopes bind provider and account ID; malformed, cross-account, oversized, or future-dated snapshots are rejected. A startup payload with no usable quota does not overwrite a prior observation. Refresh reloads the last snapshot without changing its capture time; snapshots become stale after five minutes. While a CLI is inactive, the dashboard cannot fetch a new observation. Removing a managed snapshot account deletes its snapshot, not the upstream sign-in; remove the old collector from CLI settings separately.

Use one account-bound collector stream per snapshot slot. Snapshot replacement is atomic, but concurrent collectors for the same slot are last-completion-wins rather than capture-time ordered. Their retained observation timestamp is still shown without modification. Collection rechecks the profile after writing so an overlapping account removal does not leave a recreated managed snapshot.

## Cursor team accounts

Set a team API key in the environment used to launch the local host, for example under `CURSOR_WORK_TEAM_KEY`, then choose **Cursor team spending**. Enter the environment variable name, not the secret, and the exact encoded member ID (`user_...`) from the team's documented `/teams/members` operation. A second member can reference the same team credential variable; another team uses its own variable. Subset stores only references and IDs in owner-only configuration and omits both from dashboard props and profile-list responses. The source is the [official team Admin API](https://cursor.com/docs/account/teams/admin-api).

The adapter calls only the fixed `https://api.cursor.com/teams/spend` endpoint with Basic authentication and bounded pagination/response size/timeouts. It reports on-demand `spendCents`, the included usage value derived from `overallSpendCents - spendCents`, the reported enforced `effectivePerUserLimitDollars` cap, and `subscriptionCycleStart`. An absent cap or cycle end remains unknown; a spending cap is not a personal subscription quota. Authorization failures, missing members, rate limiting, and malformed responses are isolated per account, without exposing credentials or upstream response text.

## Validation and release gaps

Run `npm run test --workspace=@subset/usage` and `npm run test --workspace=@subset/usage-web` after the package build, alongside root `npm run check` and `npm run build`. Root checks build the catalog and usage declarations before checking consuming apps, so they do not require pre-existing ignored `dist` exports. Tests exercise synthetic multi-account provider reads, explicit access denials, safe transport failures, separate snapshot collection, normalization, redaction, profile persistence/removal, pending-login recovery, the local CLI, and host Origin checks. These are not proof of real upstream multi-account login, installed CLI compatibility, or live Cursor API authorization. No public or external-agent availability is claimed by these additions.

## Superfunctions reuse review

Reviewed current `superfunctions-dev` source, public manifests, and README contracts on 2026-09-29, plus npm package versions. `authfn@0.3.0` is for owned session/auth flows; Codex app-server already owns this local account login. `@datafn/client@0.1.1` adds synced persistence that this slice does not need. `plugfn@0.1.0` targets third-party service connections, while this source is a local documented Codex process. `@mcpfn/core@0.0.5` is used by the isolated Outright MCP adapter; the capability itself remains host independent. `@uifn/components-svelte@0.0.1` and React equivalent were evaluated; this view currently needs only semantic HTML and a progress element, so no generic primitive dependency was added. `@superfunctions/observability@0.0.1` was evaluated; the connector avoids logging account data and has no telemetry runtime. **Package/version used in this package: none.** Gaps: hosted agent rendering, live two-account verification, and a release-ready hosted account authorization path remain.

The multi-provider extension additionally reviewed `plugfn/core` implementation, manifest and README, the provider manifest and readiness matrix, and `authfn/core` implementation, manifest and README on 2026-10-01. Published `plugfn@0.1.0` has no supported Cursor provider and requires an auth/database/encrypted persistent connection runtime; `authfn@0.3.0` owns application sessions, not externally issued team API keys or CLI snapshots. Neither is used. The local alternative remains fixed-endpoint read-only collection with environment credential references, not a competing OAuth or connection framework.

The 2026-10-08 UI update checked the current `superfunctions-dev` checkout for icon and chart packages; none is published there, so the view uses `phosphor-svelte@3.1.0` and `echarts@6.1.0` directly as narrow presentation dependencies.

The package is private. A future npm release requires the `@sub-set/` scope, versioned exports, a release process, and separate verification.

# @sub-set/usage

A local dashboard and CLI for AI subscription usage: ChatGPT (Codex), Claude, Cursor, Factory Droid, Amp, Devin, Antigravity, and logins stored by Pi, OpenCode, omp, and Hermes. It runs on your computer, binds only to `127.0.0.1`, and sends nothing to Subset.

> Status: prepared for npm, not yet published. Install from a tarball or the repository until a release is announced.

## Use

Requires Node.js 22 or later.

```sh
npx @sub-set/usage            # open the dashboard
npm install -g @sub-set/usage # or install the subset-usage command
subset-usage serve --port 4174 --no-open
subset-usage status           # current usage as JSON, read-only
```

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `serve` (default) | Starts the dashboard on `127.0.0.1` (port 4174, or the next free port) and opens it. `--port <n>` requires that port; `--no-open` skips the browser. Ctrl-C stops it. |
| `status` | Prints the normalized usage status (`@subset/usage` contract, schema version 1) and exits. |
| `collect --account <id>` | Saves a quota snapshot from a Claude Code or Antigravity status line. Installed collectors call it through a shim; you rarely run it yourself. |

## Data and permissions

- Configuration: `~/.config/subset/codex-profiles.json` (override with `SUBSET_USAGE_PROFILES_FILE`).
- Data: `~/.local/share/subset/` (override with `SUBSET_USAGE_DATA_DIR`): managed Codex homes, quota snapshots, usage history (times and percentages only), and the collector shim `bin/subset-usage-collect`.
- **Use local sign-ins** is off until you choose on the dashboard's first-run question. When on, the CLI reads, without changing or refreshing, the sign-ins Claude Code, Factory Droid, the Cursor app, Devin, Pi, OpenCode, omp, and Hermes keep on this computer, and calls the usage endpoints those tools use. Those endpoints are undocumented and may change. Tokens are never stored, logged, or sent to the page.
- Installing a collector edits that CLI's `settings.json` only when you ask, keeps a backup, and keeps your previous status line running.
- The local API accepts only same-origin requests carrying the dashboard's own header.

## Development

From the repository root, `npm run build` builds `@subset/usage`, the `apps/usage` view, and this package: `dist/cli.mjs` (bundled with rolldown, no runtime dependencies) and `web/` (a copy of `apps/usage/dist`). `npm test --workspace=@sub-set/usage` runs the CLI tests. `npm run serve --workspace=@sub-set/usage` runs the source without bundling.

## Release

Releases are tag-based. Bump `version` here, merge, then push a tag `usage-v<version>`; `.github/workflows/publish-tag.yml` installs, checks, builds, tests, packs, and publishes with the organization `NPM_TOKEN`. `scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs` refuses a tag whose version or package name does not match. Verify the published package (`npx @sub-set/usage@<version> --version`, then a real `serve`) before listing it as available anywhere.

== .data.instructions
# Linear Backlog Architect

Shape a product outcome or an existing Linear backlog into executable, reviewable issues for an agent implementation loop. Use this skill when asked to decompose a feature, audit issue scope, sequence sub-issues, or prepare issues for automated delivery. For an idea that only needs durable capture and product/architecture documents, use `21n/add-to-backlog` instead.

## Modes and authority

- **Plan or audit:** read the relevant repository, architecture, issue descriptions/discussion, existing backlog, and loop configuration. Return a proposed issue tree, dependency graph, and readiness findings without changing Linear or the execution queue.
- **Publish:** when the user has asked to create or revise issues, make the approved outcome concrete in Linear. This request authorizes the corresponding issue, document, and relation writes; do not ask again for routine details that are supported by the project context. If the destination or a product decision needed to write truthful acceptance criteria remains ambiguous, ask only about that decision.
- **Queue:** update a delivery loop's ordered issue/dependency configuration only when the user has also authorized adding this work to that loop. Publishing issues does not itself start implementation, dispatch cards, merge PRs, or mark issues Done.

Use Composio CLI for all Linear reads and writes in the `21n` workspace, with the configured account when selecting Linear tools. Before issue creation or document association, retrieve the published `21n/create-and-associate-linear-issue@1.0.0` skill and follow its destination, duplicate, partial-write, and read-back rules. Use the relevant Linear relation tools for parent/child and blocked-by links, then read them back. After an ambiguous write response, inspect Linear before retrying; never create a second issue to repair an uncertain first write.

## Build the delivery shape

1. Establish the outcome, current architecture and repository boundaries, decisions already made, and evidence that will establish completion. Distinguish facts, proposals, assumptions, and unresolved product choices. Preserve existing issue IDs, discussion, links, and any active PR scope.
2. Use a parent issue for the outcome when several PR-sized pieces belong together. The parent describes the integrated result and completion gate; executable children describe one coherent behavior or invariant each. Do not dispatch an umbrella issue as if it were another implementation slice. For a genuinely single-PR outcome, one issue is enough.
3. Split where pieces have different behavior, subsystem ownership, validation, release risk, or review context. Keep a tightly coupled invariant together when splitting would leave an invalid intermediate state. Do not split by arbitrary file or line counts, and do not create bookkeeping children that cannot be independently verified.
4. For every executable issue, write a compact contract: user/system trigger and expected behavior; scope and explicit exclusions; owned boundary and relevant interfaces/invariants; concrete acceptance checks with observable evidence; verification surface (unit, integration, UI, CI, external/manual); dependencies; and any migration, rollback, or rollout gate that actually applies. Name a deferred manual acceptance issue explicitly rather than treating unrun manual testing as proof.
5. Draw a directed acyclic graph of **real prerequisites**. Use Linear blocked-by relations for required ordering; parent/child links are hierarchy, not dependency. Distinguish a preferred execution order from a blocker. Parallel children need stable shared interfaces, compatible base branches, and a stated integration point. If stacked PRs are necessary, identify the base and the merge/rebase sequence.
6. Carry cross-cutting requirements into each affected child's acceptance criteria and, where needed, a final integrated acceptance issue. Do not put all implementation into one broad cross-cutting ticket.

## Readiness decision

Before publishing or queueing, assess every executable issue for: a bounded, coherent PR outcome; known prerequisite contract; observable acceptance evidence; explicit deferred/external validation; no unresolved decision that would change the implementation contract; and compatibility with the current repository and loop. Mark it `ready`, `needs decision`, or `needs split`, with the reason. A parent outcome is `container`, not an executable `ready` issue. A large issue may be ready if it is one atomic invariant and the reviewer can assess it as one change.

Return an ordered table with proposed or existing issue IDs, parent, outcome, dependencies, parallelism, readiness, and verification. Include the smallest useful issue descriptions, a dependency DAG, and any decision required from the user. For an existing backlog, propose changes only to unstarted issues by default; report active PR work separately rather than rewriting its acceptance contract mid-review.

## Publishing and verification

Search the chosen project/team for equivalent issues first. Preserve a supplied existing issue and its discussion; if a likely duplicate is found for a new issue, resolve reuse versus distinct creation with the user as the shared Linear skill requires. Create or amend only the issues in scope, then add parent/child and blocked-by relations. Confirm each issue's ID, URL, team, project, state, description, parent, dependencies, and required links by reading Linear back. Check the team setting for parent/sub-issue auto-close before relying on a manual completion gate; if auto-close could mark a parent Done without the owner's go, report that conflict and do not claim the gate is protected.

For the shared Hermes Linear loop at `/Users/serro/Documents/dev/n/agent/automation/linear-loop`, queue only executable ready issues, keep the existing config's order/dependency conventions, run its config and focused tests, and dry-run the coordinator. Preserve existing dirty work and active cards. Do not start the coordinator or dispatch new work unless that action was requested. Report the published IDs, verified relations, queue changes, tests, and any remaining unverified external behavior.

# Create and Associate Linear Issue

Provide the shared Linear mutation layer for parent skills and agent workflows. Resolve the correct destination, create or reuse one issue, associate required artifacts, recover partial writes, and verify the resulting Linear state.

## Handoff contract

Require the parent workflow to provide:

- `operation`: `create_or_reuse` or `associate_existing`;
- `purpose`: why the issue or association is needed;
- `destinationHints`: explicit project, team, repository, product, or existing Linear context;
- `desiredState`: semantic intent such as `backlog` or `active_development`;
- `issue`: title and evidence-based description when creating;
- `existingIssue`: issue identifier when associating with an existing issue;
- `associations`: required documents, commits, pull requests, deployments, or other references;
- `completionRequirements`: facts and links that must be verified before success.

Do not start Linear mutations when the handoff is missing information required to choose a unique destination or truthful state.

## 1. Resolve the destination

Use the Linear connector for every Linear read and write.

Resolve the project and team in this order:

1. project or team explicitly named by the user;
2. association already established in the current task or supplied issue;
3. repository or product ownership that maps to one Linear project and team.

Use the selected project's associated team. Never choose by name similarity alone. If the project is missing, spans multiple plausible teams, or conflicts with the handoff, ask the user before creating or moving anything.

## 2. Prevent duplicates and unsafe retries

- If `existingIssue` is supplied, retrieve it and verify its team, project, and state before associating anything.
- Before creating, search the resolved project and team for an equivalent active issue.
- If a likely duplicate exists, ask whether to reuse it or create a distinct issue; do not silently duplicate or merge work.
- After a timeout or ambiguous mutation response, read Linear state before retrying.
- Once an issue identifier is observed, preserve and reuse it for the rest of the workflow.

## 3. Create or reuse the issue

For `create_or_reuse`:

- Create one concise, outcome-oriented issue in the resolved team and attach it to the resolved project.
- Map `desiredState` to the team's truthful workflow state.
  - For `backlog`, use Backlog; if unavailable, use the nearest unstarted or triage state and disclose the substitution.
  - For `active_development`, use the team's active state such as In Progress.
- Do not invent priority, assignee, estimate, cycle, deadline, or completion state.
- Create the issue before documents or references that require its identifier.
- Do not place links in the initial description until their targets exist.

For `associate_existing`, do not create another issue.

Capture the issue identifier and direct URL.

## 4. Create and associate artifacts

Process associations in dependency order.

### Documents

- Create each required Linear document only after the issue identifier exists.
- Include the issue identifier and a backlink to the issue in every document.
- Associate each document with the issue using Linear's supported relationship or a visible issue link.
- After all documents exist, update the issue description or a clearly visible comment with their direct links.
- If Linear cannot create or associate the required documents, stop and report the capability limitation. Do not substitute local files or claim completion.

### Existing references

For commits, pull requests, deployments, or existing documents:

- Verify the supplied reference exists when the connector exposes that information.
- Link it to the existing issue without changing unrelated issue fields.
- Never invent a hash, URL, deployment result, or review state.

## 5. Recover partial writes

If the issue exists but an association fails:

- keep the same issue identifier;
- record or preserve an explicit `association incomplete` status in the issue when possible;
- retry only the missing association after checking current Linear state;
- do not recreate successful documents or duplicate issue comments;
- report the partial result and exact blocker if recovery cannot complete.

## 6. Verify and return a receipt

Read the issue and every required association back through Linear. Confirm:

- issue identifier and URL;
- team and project;
- actual workflow state and any disclosed substitution;
- issue title and essential description;
- every required association and backlink;
- no unresolved partial-write marker;
- every parent-supplied completion requirement.

Return a structured receipt containing those facts, plus assumptions, substitutions, and anything not verified. Do not report success until all blocking completion requirements pass.

## Integrity rules

- Preserve the parent workflow's authorization boundaries; this skill does not authorize implementation, commits, pushes, deployment, assignments, or dates.
- Keep issue content evidence-based and consistent with associated artifacts.
- Do not expose secrets, tokens, private logs, customer-sensitive information, or unnecessary personal data.
- Never fabricate destination mappings, issue identifiers, links, states, associations, or verification results.

content.text:
Everything you asked for is done. `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass, and all 128 tests pass (93 library, 35 CLI). Nothing is committed, tagged or published.

**CLI package `@sub-set/usage`** (in `packages/usage-cli`)
- The server and account code moved here from `apps/usage`, so packages no longer import from apps. `apps/usage` now holds only the Svelte UI. The CLI's build bundles the shared `@subset/usage` code into `dist/cli.mjs` and copies the built UI into `web/`.
- It needs Node 22 or later and has no runtime dependencies. I bundled with rolldown, which Vite already brings in, instead of adding esbuild.
- Commands: `subset-usage serve|status|collect`, with `--port`, `--no-open`, `--help` and `--version`. The default port is 4174 and moves to the next free port if that one is taken.
- I tested a packed tarball installed into a scratch prefix: the page loads, an API call without the new header is refused, and the collector shim is written.
- Status-line collectors now call a stable shim at `~/.local/share/subset/bin/subset-usage-collect`. `serve` rewrites it on each start, and also updates collectors installed with an older command, but only where the settings file still holds that exact collector.
  - **This already ran on your machine:** your `~/.claude/settings.json` status line now calls the shim. It had pointed at `apps/usage/server.mjs`, which no longer exists.
- Two security changes:
  - **API guard:** every API call needs an `X-Subset-Request: 1` header, and requests the browser marks as cross-site or same-site are refused.
  - **First-run consent:** local sign-ins stay off until the user answers a question on the dashboard. Your saved choice (on) is unchanged. The banner itself wasn't checked in a browser, because your machine already has a saved answer.
- The preview is running again at `http://127.0.0.1:4174`. All 10 cards read OK with your real accounts, and the ChatGPT card shows OpenCode, omp and Pi as "also in".

**Publish workflow**
- `.github/workflows/publish-tag.yml` follows the Superfunctions one: a tag like `usage-v0.1.0` triggers it, and you can also run it by hand.
- It installs and builds from the repo root, because the CLI bundles private workspace code.
- It then checks, tests, packs and publishes using the org `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
- The tag-checking script refuses a version or package-name mismatch, or a package not marked public.
- `scripts/check-workspaces.mjs` now also checks that public packages are listed in `release-packages.json` and don't depend at runtime on private workspaces.

**Review findings:** I fixed every finding from both reviews:
- **Failed reads:** a failed read no longer erases history. An empty live Claude result falls back to the collected snapshot.
- **Fewer reads:** each tool's login store is read once per refresh. Harness and Cursor reads now run in parallel.
- **Concurrency:** preference writes are queued. Two sign-ins can no longer start at once.
- **Account identity:** cached results are keyed by the signed-in email, so switching sign-ins can't show the previous account's numbers.
  - The harness fallback no longer overrides an account Codex reports as blocked, and keeps its errors.
  - A custom default Claude directory now gets its own sign-in.
- **Collectors:** replacing another account's collector keeps your original status line, and the first settings backup is preserved.
- **Trend history keys:** labels are now consistent across sources.
- **Local sign-ins:**
  - The stored-logins list returns nothing while local sign-ins are off.
  - The exception text in `AGENTS.md`, the Settings copy and the docs now name every tool that's read: Claude, Factory Droid, Cursor, Devin, Pi, OpenCode, omp, Hermes and the Antigravity email.

**Linear** (21n account, Subset team and project, all in Backlog)
- [SET-14](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-14/deliver-subset-usage-as-a-macos-menu-bar-app-tauri) is the parent, linked to SET-1 as related.
- [SET-15](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-15/run-the-usage-runtime-inside-a-tauri-menu-bar-shell) runs the usage server inside a Tauri menu-bar shell. It needs a decision first: ship Node alongside the app, or port the server to Rust.
- [SET-16](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-16/show-usage-status-in-the-menu-bar-icon-and-menu) shows usage in the menu-bar icon and menu. It's blocked by SET-15.
- [SET-17](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-17/sign-notarize-and-release-the-macos-menu-bar-app) covers signing, notarization and release. It's blocked by SET-15 and SET-16, and needs Apple Developer ID credentials.
- I read the parent, blocking and related links back from Linear and they're correct.
- I couldn't read the team's setting for auto-closing parent issues; the API returned null. So check that SET-14 can't close itself before the clean-machine install check in its description has passed.

To release, merge this work and push the tag `usage-v0.1.0`. Then verify `npx @sub-set/usage@0.1.0` before listing it anywhere.

I re-ran the review on the current working tree. Since the last pass the code has moved into a new packages/usage-cli package, and there's now a publish workflow and release scripts. Nine of the ten earlier findings are fixed. The tenth was resolved by changing AGENTS.md instead of the code, and that change is now the top finding. Nothing was edited.

Earlier findings

I checked these against the code myself:
1. History wiped on a failed read: fixed. History now starts from what's already recorded, so an empty read no longer deletes anything.
2. Empty Claude result replacing the snapshot: fixed. The live result is only used if it has windows or the snapshot has none (server.mjs:122).
3. Unserialized preference writes: fixed. They now go through their own write queue (accounts.mjs:85).
4. "opus" vs "Opus" label: fixed. The live labels are now capitalized to match the snapshot.
5. Stored sign-ins for unapproved tools: see the first new finding below.
6. /api/stored-logins ignoring the off switch: fixed. It returns nothing while local sign-ins are off.
7. Cross-site GET requests: fixed. Every /api/ request now needs an x-subset-request header and is refused when Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site or same-site.
8. Harness logins read one at a time: fixed. They're now read in parallel.
9. Cursor reads one at a time: fixed. They're now read in parallel.
10. Docs: fixed. The usage README has a Superfunctions section, and the root README and docs/architecture.md now describe Cursor support.

New findings

Most important
1. AGENTS.md was rewritten to permit the new readers (AGENTS.md:72). The exception the owner directed covered only the Claude Code and Factory Droid sign-ins, on by default. The diff extends it to Cursor, Devin, Pi, OpenCode, omp, Hermes and Antigravity, and turns the setting off by default (accounts.mjs:349). The new text also says adding a tool "needs the owner's direction". Only you can confirm whether the owner actually directed this; if not, those readers break the rule.
2. A retried "use a reset" can spend a second Codex reset (apps/usage/src/App.svelte:320). Each click makes a new idempotency key. If the first request succeeds but its response is lost, clicking again redeems another reset. Keeping the same key for retries of the same action fixes it.
3. status isn't read-only (packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:84). status() calls ensureDefaultClaude(), which can add a claude_default profile, and it also writes usage-history.json. AGENTS.md requires status --json to be read-only.

Wrong account shown
4. Harness logins are grouped by email alone (packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:152). Logins for different ChatGPT workspaces under the same email (say, Personal and Team) collapse into one card. One workspace's quota disappears, or its numbers show on the other card.
5. The Factory local sign-in overrides a profile's configured key (packages/usage/src/factory.ts:131). When local sign-ins are on, a profile set up with account B's key shows account A's limits. Devin uses the opposite order, so the two providers behave inconsistently.
6. Devin falls back to the default sign-in when the profile's key is missing (packages/usage/src/devin.ts:82). If the profile's key variable isn't set, it uses the default local login instead. The "Work" card then shows the personal account's quota as OK rather than an error.
7. Antigravity accounts share one settings.json (packages/usage-cli/src/accounts.mjs:408). Installing one account's collector replaces the other's, and the dashboard's "Reinstall" button just swaps them back. Only one account ever collects.

Smaller issues
8. Stale results after changing settings (App.svelte:190). refresh() does nothing if a refresh is already running. Turning on local sign-ins or using a reset mid-refresh can leave old results on screen until the next auto-refresh, up to 30 minutes later.
9. claude auth status runs on every refresh (server.mjs:111). It runs once per Claude profile, with a timeout of up to 10 seconds, even when local sign-ins are off and the result isn't used. It isn't cached.
10. An option name doesn't match (accounts.mjs:57). readClaudeAuth passes defaultConfigDir, but the reader only accepts builtInConfigDir, so the option is silently ignored. server.mjs also works out the default Claude directory separately, so the two can drift apart.

The original eight findings are resolved in the scenarios reported. I found related account-identity gaps plus new CLI and release issues, with mocked reproductions confirming the runtime cases. All 63 reviewed file hashes still match the starting snapshot.
Found five actionable issues:

1. **\[P1\] Manual releases can publish a different commit from the requested tag.** .github/workflows/publish-tag.yml:30 checks out the dispatch ref, while `release_tag` only selects and validates the package version. Dispatching from `main` can publish untagged changes under an existing release version. Checkout and verify the requested tag before building.
2. **\[P2\] Old Claude snapshots can be attributed to a newly signed-in account.** packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:113 adds the current auth email to previously collected quota. After switching accounts, disabling local sign-ins or losing live credentials returns the old account’s windows under the new email. A mocked reproduction confirmed this. Bind snapshots to the observed identity or invalidate them when identity changes.
3. **\[P2\] Cache identity checks remain incomplete.** packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:107 uses an empty identity when a stored login lacks an email. Replacing that login still returns the previous quota for two minutes; account IDs, token changes, and sign-out flags are ignored. Other provider caches also remain keyed only by profile. Validate the current credential state before cache reuse and use a stable account identity.
4. **\[P2\] Separate profile configurations overwrite each other’s collector shim.** packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:208 uses one shim per data directory but embeds the active profiles-file path. Starting configuration B overwrites the shim already installed for A, redirecting A’s collectors to B’s profiles. A mocked reproduction confirmed the overwrite. Give each configuration its own shim or preserve its binding in the collector command.
5. **\[P2\] The advertised read-only `status` command persists configuration.** packages/usage-cli/src/server.mjs:84 calls `ensureDefaultClaude()`, which writes an automatically discovered profile. Keep discovery transient for `status`, or reserve persistence for an explicit account operation.

All eight previous findings were rechecked. The revised provider authorization, disabled-store listing, custom Claude directory selection, original live-cache mismatch, blocked fallback, collector restoration, history retention, and concurrent-login cases are resolved.

I fixed every valid finding from both re-reviews. One needs your confirmation rather than a code change: the AGENTS.md exception (re-review 1, finding 1). `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass, and all 129 tests pass (93 library, 36 CLI). Your live dashboard still shows the same 10 accounts with no errors, and nothing is committed or tagged.

**Needs your confirmation: AGENTS.md exception.** I widened it last round because you asked for those readers in this conversation: personal Cursor, Devin, Amp, Pi, OpenCode, omp, Hermes, and the Antigravity email. The change to "off until the user answers a first-run question" came from my recommendation, which you approved, though you had earlier asked for "on by default". If either isn't what you want, tell me and I'll revert that part.

**Fixed:**
- **Manual publish could use the wrong commit:** a manual run of `publish-tag.yml` now checks out the requested tag. It also fails unless the checked-out commit is that tag's commit.
- **`status` wasn't read-only:** it now writes nothing. A signed-in default Claude account is shown without being saved, and no history or sign-in records are written. The dashboard server still saves these as before.
- **A retried Codex reset could spend a second reset:** a retry now reuses the same idempotency key until a response arrives, for up to 10 minutes.
- **Different workspaces under one email were merged:** harness logins (Pi, OpenCode, omp, Hermes) are now grouped by email *and* ChatGPT workspace. They join a direct ChatGPT card only when the plans match, so Personal and Team stay separate. That workspace and plan come from the stored login's token, read locally.
- **Factory and Devin used the wrong account:** an account set up with an API key variable now always uses that key. If the variable isn't set, it shows an error instead of quietly reading your default local sign-in.
- **Antigravity accounts swapped collectors:** Antigravity has one settings file, so a second account's collector install is now refused. That account shows "Used by another account" instead of offering a Reinstall that swaps them.
- **Old Claude snapshots shown under a new account:** the server now records which email each Claude account was signed in as, in `claude-identities.json`. After a sign-in change, earlier snapshots aren't shown under the new account; the card says it's waiting for a new snapshot.
- **Stale cached results after replacing a stored login:** harness results are now cached against a hash of the stored login (account, workspace and token), so a replaced or signed-out login is read again immediately.
- **Two configurations overwrote each other's collector shim:** a custom profiles file now gets its own shim (`subset-usage-collect-<hash>`). Your default setup keeps `subset-usage-collect`.
- **Stale results after changing settings:** a refresh requested while another is running now runs once more afterwards.
- **`claude auth status` on every refresh:** results are now cached per directory for 60 seconds. It still runs when local sign-ins are off, because its result supplies the card's email and signed-in state.
- **Option name mismatch:** the ignored `defaultConfigDir` option is removed. The built-in `~/.claude` directory is now defined in one place.

**Not fully fixed:** the Factory, personal Cursor, Devin and Amp caches are still keyed by account only. After switching sign-in in one of those tools, the previous account's numbers can show for up to 1–2 minutes before the cache expires. Fixing it means reading each tool's credentials before every cache hit; say if you want that.

The dashboard preview is running again at http://127.0.0.1:4174.

## Summary

Pilot for [SET-1](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-1/pilot-a-reusable-usage-status-dashboard): a local dashboard for AI subscription usage, packaged as a CLI.

- **`@subset/usage`** (private): the usage contract (schema v1), read-only provider readers, local history, and the shared Svelte dashboard view.
  - Readers: Codex/ChatGPT via app-server, Claude (status-line snapshots plus the live OAuth usage read), Cursor team (Admin API) and personal (desktop sign-in), Factory Droid, Amp, Devin, Antigravity, and Pi/OpenCode/omp/Hermes stored logins.
- **`apps/usage`** (private): the standalone UI, covering the dashboard, settings, account dialogs, collector setup, and a first-run local sign-ins question.
- **`@sub-set/usage`** (`packages/usage-cli`, public, not yet published): `subset-usage serve|status|collect`.
  - Bundled with rolldown; Node 22 or later; no runtime dependencies.
  - The server binds to 127.0.0.1 only, and every API call needs an `X-Subset-Request` header.
  - `status` writes nothing.
  - Collectors call a stable shim, one per configuration.
- **Release**: `.github/workflows/publish-tag.yml`, modelled on Superfunctions. A `usage-v<version>` tag checks out and verifies that tag, then checks, builds, tests, packs, and publishes with `NPM_TOKEN`.
  - `scripts/resolve-release-tag.mjs` refuses a version or name mismatch.
  - `scripts/check-workspaces.mjs` checks public packages against `release-packages.json`.
- **Docs and rules**:
  - AGENTS.md: local sign-ins exception, owner-directed on 2026-10-08.
  - Root README and `docs/architecture.md`.
  - Package READMEs, including the Superfunctions reuse review.
- **Catalog**: usage moves from `planned` to `building`. `availableSurfaces` stays empty.

## Review notes

- Two review passes were addressed:
  - History retention and identity-safe caches.
  - Claude snapshot identity binding and the shared Antigravity collector.
  - Configured-key precedence for Factory and Devin; workspace-aware harness merging.
  - Codex reset idempotency.
  - Serialized writes.
- Known limitation: the Factory, personal Cursor, Devin, and Amp caches are keyed by account. After a sign-in switch, the previous account's values can show for up to 1–2 minutes.
- **Reviewer confirmation needed:** the AGENTS.md exception covers Claude Code, Factory Droid, the Cursor app, Devin, Pi, OpenCode, omp, Hermes, and the Antigravity email. Local sign-ins stay off until the user answers the first-run question.

## Testing

- `npm run check` and `npm run build` pass.
- `npm test` passes: 93 library tests and 36 CLI tests.
- The packed tarball, installed into a scratch prefix, serves the page, refuses API calls without the guard header, and writes the collector shim.
- Live local run against real accounts across all providers.
- Not verified:
  - npm publication (no tag pushed).
  - The workflow on GitHub.
  - Agent-host embedding.
  - The first-run banner in a browser.
  - The macOS menu-bar app ([SET-14](https://linear.app/21n/issue/SET-14/deliver-subset-usage-as-a-macos-menu-bar-app-tauri), backlog).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
